\section[o rendimento]{o rendimento — the income; the yield}

\label{lesson:PT-C391-rendimento}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for guilty, then the Portuguese for innocent.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o rendimento}
\textbf{o rendimento} — \textquotedblleft{}the income; the yield\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O rendimento da família subiu este ano.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The family's income went up this year.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Rendimento mensal} — monthly income.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{rendimento} is built on \emph{render} \textquotedblleft{}to yield, to give back\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Vulgar Latin \emph{rendere}, a form of Latin \emph{reddere} \textquotedblleft{}to give back\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o rendimento}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o rendimento}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{o rendimento}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for guilty, then the Portuguese for innocent, then say \emph{o rendimento} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does o rendimento mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The income; the yield\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[o orçamento]{o orçamento — the budget; the quote, the estimate}

\label{lesson:PT-C391-orcamento}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for innocent, then the Portuguese for the income.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o orçamento}
\textbf{o orçamento} — \textquotedblleft{}the budget; the quote, the estimate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O nosso orçamento para as férias é pequeno.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Our budget for the holidays is small.}
\end{quote}

Also a builder's quote: \emph{pedir um orçamento}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{orçamento} is built on \emph{orçar} \textquotedblleft{}to estimate\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), which EtymDB traces to Italian \emph{orzare}, from Vulgar Latin \emph{ortiāre} \textquotedblleft{}to raise\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{orīrī} \textquotedblleft{}to rise\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o orçamento}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{o orçamento}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for innocent, then the Portuguese for the income, then say \emph{o orçamento} again
\end{itemize}

\section[a despesa]{a despesa — the expense, the spending}

\label{lesson:PT-C391-despesa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the income, then the Portuguese for the budget.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a despesa}
\textbf{a despesa} — \textquotedblleft{}the expense, the spending\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
As despesas da casa são altas.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The household expenses are high.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Dividir as despesas} — to share the costs.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{despesa} goes back to Old Portuguese \emph{despesa} (EtymDB), usually traced to Late Latin \emph{dispēnsa} \textquotedblleft{}things paid out\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{dispendere} \textquotedblleft{}to weigh out\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{pendere} \textquotedblleft{}to weigh\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a despesa}, once more

\section[a prestação]{a prestação — the instalment; the performance}

\label{lesson:PT-C391-prestacao}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the budget, then the Portuguese for the expense.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a prestação}
\textbf{a prestação} — \textquotedblleft{}the instalment; the performance\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Pago o carro em prestações mensais.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I pay for the car in monthly instalments.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Às prestações} — in instalments. Also a performance at work or in sport.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{prestação} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{praestātiō} \textquotedblleft{}a payment, a guarantee\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), on \emph{praestāre} \textquotedblleft{}to stand before, to provide\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{stāre} \textquotedblleft{}to stand\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[a poupança]{a poupança — the saving; savings}

\label{lesson:PT-C391-poupanca}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the expense, then the Portuguese for the instalment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a poupança}
\textbf{a poupança} — \textquotedblleft{}the saving; savings\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Usei as minhas poupanças para comprar um carro.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I used my savings to buy a car.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Conta poupança} — savings account.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{poupança} is built on \emph{poupar} \textquotedblleft{}to save\textquotedblright{}, which is inherited from Latin \emph{palpāre} \textquotedblleft{}to touch softly, to stroke\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short): to handle money gently.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
